Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 81, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

.

Tafsir of Surah (Kawwarat) [At-Takwir]

It is Meccan.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated from ʿAbd Allah ibn Bujayr, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Yazid al-San'ani, who said: I heard Ibn ʿUmar say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever would like to look upon the Day of Resurrection as if he were seeing it with his own eye, let him recite: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, and ﴿When the sky is cleft asunder﴾, and (When the sky is split open)."

He (may Allah be pleased with him) said: This hadith was related to us by Abu ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Qaffal; Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Sinji al-Makhhal related to us; al-ʿAbbas ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzim al-ʿAnbari related to us; ʿAbd al-Razzaq related to us.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: its light has gone away.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, who said: "Kuwwirat" means it was thrown away.

And from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "kuwwira al-ʿimama" (the turban was wound up), and the meaning is that it was rolled up and gathered together and cast away.

And His saying: ﴿When the stars fall, scattered﴾ — meaning: they will be scattered and fall down. In some tafsir works it is mentioned that the stars are in lamps of light suspended from the lowest heaven by chains in the hands of the angels. When the Day of Resurrection comes, the chains will drop from the hands of the angels, and the stars will be scattered.

It is also narrated that the people of the earths will hear a great clamor from the falling of the stars upon the earth.

Its saying: ﴿And when the mountains are set in motion﴾, meaning: they are set in motion and become like a mirage. It is also said: they are crushed into fine dust and become like scattered particles of dust. The verse is in the same sense as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them solid, while they pass away as the clouds pass away﴾.

And His saying: ﴿And when the pregnant camels are left neglected﴾. Al-'ushshar (the pregnant camels) — its singular is 'ushara', and it is the she-camel that has reached ten months of her pregnancy, and she is the best of camels and the dearest of them to their owners. Ta'til (neglect) means leaving them unattended and abandoned, with no herdsman to tend them. This does not happen except on the Day of Resurrection. The meaning is that every person will be preoccupied with himself, away from everything, even if it was dear to him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 81, verse 5:

And His saying: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾ has two interpretations. The first: the meaning is that they die, and hashr (gathering) is the collecting together, so it is as if they are gathered together in death. The second view, which is the more apparent, is that their gathering is their being brought back to life on the Day of Resurrection.

It has been reported in the well-known hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Retribution will be taken for the hornless sheep from the horned sheep."

And from Ibn ʿAbbas, he said: "Every creature will be gathered, even the flies."

And His saying: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾ (wa-idha al-bihar sujjirat). Al-Hasan said: they will be dried up. And from him (al-Hasan) it is also reported that he said: they will overflow, i.e., some of them will be made to enter into others.

And it is related from Ka'b al-Ahbar that "sujjirat" means they will be filled with fire.

And Shimr ibn 'Atiyyah said: they will be kindled as the oven (tannur) is kindled.

.

It is related from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab that 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) asked a man from among the Jews about Jahannam (Hell), and he said: "It is the sea." 'Ali said: "I do not think he is anything but truthful," and then he recited the words of the Most High: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾.

And it is related from some of them: that the Mediterranean Sea (bahr al-Rum) is in the middle of the earth, and at its bottom are wells of copper that are sealed shut. When the Day of Resurrection comes, they will be set ablaze as fire. And from this is the saying of the Most High: ﴿And the sea that is filled (al-bahr al-masjur)﴾, which we have already explained. It is permissible to combine these sayings, so it is said: the seas will enter into one another and become one sea, then it will overflow and dry up, then it will be filled with fire.

And His saying: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. Al-Sha'bi said: the bodies are paired with the souls. It was also said: they are joined with their deeds.

And it is related from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: the righteous is with the righteous, and the wicked is with the wicked.

And it is related from some of them: the believers are paired with the wide-eyed houris (al-ḥūr al-ʿīn), and the disbelievers with the devils (al-shayāṭīn).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 81, verses 8–9:

﴿And when the girl buried alive is asked for what sin she was killed﴾. Al-Mawuduh (the girl buried alive): it is the child, whom the people of the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance) would kill. When one of them had a son born to him, he left him; and when a daughter was born to him, he buried her alive.

Some of them mentioned:

That a woman, when the pains of labour seized her, would dig a pit and sit over it. If she gave birth to a boy, she kept him; and if she gave birth to a girl, she threw her into the pit. Some of them would leave the girl until she grew strong, then say to her mother: "Perfume her, adorn her." He would dig a well in the desert, take her with himself, order her to look into the well, then push her from behind into the well and shovel the dust over her. They used to do this either out of fear of poverty, or to repel shame and out of pride in themselves.

His saying: ﴿for what sin she was killed﴾ is a question of rebuke to the one who buries; for the answer to this question would be that she says: "I was killed without any sin."

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak and a group read: "And when the buried girl asks for what sin she was killed," and the meaning is known.

Some of them mentioned in its interpretation that she will come covered in blood, clinging to her mother's breast, and saying: "O Lord, this is my mother, and she has killed me."

Know that many reports have come that the children of the polytheists are servants of the people of Paradise.

Ibn 'Abbas used to say: whoever says that the buried girl is in the Fire has lied, and he recited this verse.

From the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "I asked my Lord about the heedless ones among the offspring of mankind, and He gave them to me."

And from him (ﷺ) that he was asked about the children of the polytheists, and he said: "They are servants of the people of Paradise."

Other reports have come that the children of the polytheists are in the Fire, and we have mentioned some of that earlier. And from him (ﷺ) that he said to 'A'ishah: "If I wished, I would make you hear their wailing in the Fire." And from him (ﷺ) that he said: "The one who buries and the one buried are in the Fire." It is also established, by the narration of Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about the children of the polytheists, and he said: "God knows best what they were doing."

The better course is to withhold judgment and entrust the knowledge of that to God Most High, and they are under His will: He does with them what He wills.

Know that there were among the Arabs those who would preserve buried children, by which they [would] flee from their fathers.

And al-Farazdaq boasted, saying:

(And from us is the one who prevented the burying-women, so he revived the buried one and it was not buried.)

He said this about his grandfather Sa'sa'ah ibn Mujashi'.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when the pages are unrolled﴾, meaning: before all creation. Some of them will be given their record in their right hand, and some of them will be given it in their left hand.

And His saying: ﴿And when the sky is stripped away﴾. Ibn Mas'ud read it as "قشطت", and the two have the same meaning, like "الكافور والقافور" (al-kafur and al-qafur, both meaning camphor).

And His saying: ﴿كشطت﴾ means uprooted (qula'at). It was said that it means pulled off (nuzi'at).

And His saying: ﴿And when the Blazing Fire is kindled﴾ means: it is set ablaze; and it is kindled time after time, so the statement is sound on this reading.

Qatadah said: "Its fuel is the wrath of God and the sins of the children of Adam."
And His saying: ﴿And when Paradise is brought near﴾ — that is, it is brought close and made nigh; and it is for the God-fearing (al-muttaqun).

And His saying: ﴿Every soul will know what it has brought forward﴾. Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: To this the speech has been directed, and the meaning of this has been related from Ibn 'Abbas.

The meaning: when these things occur, every soul will know what it has brought forward, that is, of good and evil.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 81, verse 15:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So I swear by the stars that recede﴾. ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) said: They are five planets: Bahrām (Mars), ʿUṭārid (Mercury), Zuḥal (Saturn), al-Zuhra (Venus), and al-Mushtarī (Jupiter). Some of them also included the sun and the moon in this.

And it is reported from some of them that they are all the stars.

As for His words ﴿al-khunnas﴾, it means: they disappear in their course. It was also said: they disappear during the day and appear at night. It was also said: they turn back in their course from the west, and this is evident in the five planets.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 81, verse 16:

And His saying: ﴿By the stars that recede, that run and hide﴾. That is, the female wild cows that travel and hide (al-kunus), and al-kunus means those that conceal themselves from sight.

It is also said: [they are the stars] that set, and it is also said: [they are the stars] of the daytime.

These stars are the ones the astrologers (al-munajjimun) call "the wandering stars" (al-mutahayyira). They are distinctive in their motion, unlike all other stars: for all other stars move from east to west, whereas these move from west to east. The astrologers attribute the events in the world to them. We, however, disavow to God Most High this belief, and we refer all matters to God Most High. The stars are only signs, indications, and things subjected [to God's command], created for meanings that we have mentioned before.

There is another view regarding the verse: that al-khunus are the wild cattle.

ʿAmr ibn Shurahbil said: Ibn Masʿud said to me: "You are an Arab people, so what is the meaning of ﴿al-khunus al-jawar al-kunus﴾?" ʿAmr said: "They are the wild cattle." Ibn Masʿud said: "I also think so," and this is also one of the two reports from Ibn ʿAbbas. But the first view is the well-known one.

According to this view, al-khunus are those with small noses, and al-kunus [derives] from their concealing themselves in their lairs.

And His saying: ﴿By the night when it draws close﴾, meaning: it approached with its darkness. It was also said: it withdrew. This is among the words with opposite meanings (al-addad, words that carry two contradictory senses).

The first meaning is the well-known one.
And His saying: ﴿By the dawn when it breathes out﴾ means: it appeared and rose. It was also said: it rose high.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger﴾, meaning: a word brought down by a noble messenger, i.e., noble in the sight of the One who sent him, and he is Jibril (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him).

And some have taken the verse to refer to what Jibril (peace be upon him) brought to the Messenger, other than the Qur'an.

On this view, it is permissible to say: "It is the word of Jibril."

It was also said: the saying ﴿a noble messenger﴾ refers to Muhammad. But the first view is the well-known one.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 81, verse 20:

And His saying: ﴿Possessor of strength, esteemed by the Possessor of the Throne, obeyed [there, and trustworthy]﴾. It is reported in a khabar (report) that the Prophet asked Jibril about his strength and his trustworthiness.

He said: "As for my strength, Allah the Exalted sent me to the cities of Lut, which are four cities, and in each city there were four hundred thousand fighters, besides the offspring. I inserted my wing beneath them and lifted them up to the lowest heaven, until the people of the lowest heaven heard the barking of dogs and the crowing of roosters. Then I overturned them."

"As for my trustworthiness, I did not pass on what I was commanded to anyone other than Him."

And His saying: ﴿Makin﴾ (esteemed) means standing or rank with Allah the Exalted.

And "Dhu al-Arsh" (Possessor of the Throne) is Allah the Exalted.

And His saying: ﴿Obeyed, and trustworthy﴾. In the exegesis, it means that the angels obey him in what he commands them.

It has also been said: its meaning is that he said to Ridwan, keeper of the Gardens, on the night of the Mi'raj: "Open the gate for Muhammad," and he opened it.

And he said to Malik, keeper of the Fire: "Open the gate for Muhammad," and he opened it. [Note: the text reads "اللّباب", likely a scribal error for "الباب", the gate.]

As for His saying: ﴿trustworthy﴾, we have already mentioned it.

It has also been said regarding the meaning of trustworthiness (amanah) that he lifts seventy veils without seeking permission.

And it has been said: he enters seventy veils of light without seeking permission.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 81, verse 22:

The Most High's words, ﴿And your companion is not a madman﴾, mean: the Messenger.

It is related from ʿAṭiyya that the Prophet of Allah asked Jibril to show him his own form as it is in the sky. He said: "That is not up to me until I seek permission from my Lord." So Allah the Most High gave him permission to do so.

When [the Prophet] saw Jibril in the form Allah had created him with, [possessing] greatness and a multitude of wings, as we have mentioned, he fainted. When the Quraysh saw him fainting, they said: "He is mad, he is mad!" So Allah the Most High sent down: ﴿And your companion is not a madman﴾.

And His saying: ﴿And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon﴾. In the tafsir it is said that it was at the rising-place of the sun, and that the one he saw was Jibril (Gabriel). We have already explained this in the surah of an-Najm (The Star).

And His saying: ﴿And he is not, concerning the unseen, one who withholds﴾ is read with the ḍād and with the ẓā'.

Ibrāhīm al-Nakha'ī said: "Ẓanīn with the ẓā' means accused (muttahham), and ḍanīn with the ḍād means stingy (bakhīl)."

Al-Naḥḥās cited it, and it is the view of a group of the exegetes. "The unseen" (al-ghayb) is the revelation (al-waḥy).
And His saying: ﴿And he is not the word of an accursed devil﴾. He said: This is because they used to say that Muhammad says what he says from the devil.
And His saying: ﴿Then where are you going?﴾ That is: where are you going, turning away from this truth which has become manifest through its proofs?
And His saying: ﴿It is none other than a reminder to the worlds﴾, meaning: a reminder and an admonition to the worlds.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 81, verse 28–29:

And His saying: ﴿For whoever among you wills to take the straight path﴾. In the tafsir it is related that when this verse was revealed, Abu Jahl said: "The matter is up to us: if we wish, we will go straight, and if we wish, we will not go straight." So Allah the Exalted revealed His saying, ﴿But you do not will except that Allah wills, the Lord of the worlds﴾, as a refutation of him.

There are many hadiths on this subject. Among them is what is narrated from Malik, from Zayd ibn Abi Anisa, that Abd al-Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn al-Khattab informed him, from Muslim ibn Yasar al-Juhani, that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) was asked about this verse: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾, the verse.

Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) being asked about it, and he said: 'Allah created Adam and passed His right hand over his back, and brought forth from it descendants. He said: I have created these for Paradise, and they will work with the works of the people of Paradise. Then He passed His hand over his back and brought forth, and said: I have created these for the Fire, and they will work with the works of the people of the Fire.' A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, then what is the point of works?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'When Allah the Exalted creates a servant for Paradise, He makes him work with the works of the people of Paradise until he dies upon the works of the people of Paradise, and so He admits him to Paradise by them. And when He creates a servant for the Fire, He makes him work with the works of the people of the Fire until he dies upon the works of the people of the Fire, and so He admits him to the Fire by them.'" And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels, and the dead had spoken to them, and We had gathered everything before them, they would not have believed unless Allah willed﴾.

And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And it is not for a soul to believe except by the permission of Allah﴾. He (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Abu Muhammad Hayyaj ibn Ubayd al-Khatibi informed us of this hadith in Makkah, saying: Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Jami' informed us, my grandfather informed us, Muhammad ibn Abdan al-Qazzaz informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, the hadith.

And Allah knows best.
